label: FP
reason: All three alerts are false positives. Alert 1 (java/xss) and Alert 2 (java/path-injection) both report sinks driven by user input ('param'), but the data flow resolves to a constant value ('bob') due to the switch statement logic in doSomething (switchTarget is always 'B'). Thus, the resolved sink value is constant, not attacker-controlled. Alert 3 (java/error-message-exposure) reports exposure of e.getMessage(), which stems from IO failures on a constant file path (TESTFILES_DIR + 'bob'), meaning the error message does not contain user input. All alerts fail to find actual exploitation paths involving user-controlled data.

evidence.note: doSomething method defines guess="ABC" and switchTarget=guess.charAt(1) which is always 'B', causing bar to be assigned "bob" instead of param
fileName is constructed as TESTFILES_DIR + bar, resolving to a constant path regardless of user input
Catch block exposes e.getMessage() and fileName to client/log, but neither contains user input as they derive from constant file path operations
